en: To mention a source or example supporting a statement.

ex.en: Please cite the book you used for your project.
Researchers often cite access to green spaces as an important factor in improving urban residents' mental health.

en: The area of land beside a river.

ex.en: We walked along the riverside after a late lunch.
Improving access to the riverside can create attractive public spaces and encourage residents to exercise outdoors.

en: A tiny piece that breaks off bread, cake, or biscuits

ex.en: A crumb fell from my toast onto the table.
Even small food scraps, such as bread crumbs, can attract pests when waste is poorly managed.

en: rising or falling at a sharp angle

ex.en: We pushed our bikes up the steep hill.
A steep rise in housing costs can force young workers to move away from major cities.

en: to prevent someone from having something they need or value

ex.en: The noisy roadworks deprived us of sleep all week.
Unequal access to technology can deprive disadvantaged students of valuable opportunities to develop essential digital skills.

en: an action, especially one that is notably good or bad

ex.en: Helping our neighbour carry groceries was a kind deed.
Recognising good deeds in schools can encourage students to take greater responsibility for their local communities.

en: to interrupt someone's activity, rest, or peace

ex.en: Please close the door quietly so you don't disturb Dad.
Construction noise can disturb nearby residents and reduce their quality of life over time.

en: To introduce a product or start an organised activity.

ex.en: Our local bakery launched a new delivery service yesterday.
Schools should launch awareness campaigns to encourage healthier eating habits and reduce food waste among students.

en: making you feel embarrassed or uncomfortable

ex.en: There was an awkward silence after I forgot her name.
Flexible working arrangements can help parents manage awkward schedules without sacrificing their career opportunities.

en: a hospital room or section for patients receiving similar care

ex.en: A nurse brought fresh blankets into the children's ward.
Expanding hospital wards alone will not improve healthcare unless sufficient trained staff are also available.

en: to increase or improve something

ex.en: A short walk can boost your energy after lunch.
Investment in reliable public transport can boost local employment and improve access to essential services.

en: to show that something exists or is likely

ex.en: These dark clouds indicate that rain is coming.
Recent surveys indicate that affordable housing remains a major concern for young adults in urban areas.

en: far better than usual

ex.en: The young violinist gave an exceptional performance last night.
Students with exceptional ability may require additional challenges to remain engaged in classroom learning.

en: The distance from a surface to the bottom.

ex.en: Check the depth before you jump into the pool.
University courses should encourage students to explore complex environmental issues in greater depth.

en: a small screen image representing a program, file, or function

ex.en: Tap the camera icon to take a quick photo.
A familiar cultural icon can attract international visitors and strengthen a city's identity in tourism campaigns.

en: involving a chance of harm, failure, or loss

ex.en: It is risky to cycle home without lights.
Investing all public funds in a single industry is risky because economic conditions can change unexpectedly.

en: The act of keeping something safe from damage or loss.

ex.en: These old photographs need careful preservation to prevent further damage.
The preservation of historic buildings can strengthen local identity while attracting visitors and supporting small businesses.

en: To control the direction in which a vehicle moves.

ex.en: She carefully steered the boat away from the rocks.
Governments can steer investment towards renewable energy by offering financial incentives and establishing clear environmental standards.

en: Related to business or intended to make money.

ex.en: This street has homes above its commercial premises.
Commercial development can create jobs, but it should not come at the expense of public green spaces.

en: Someone injured or killed in an accident, conflict, or disaster.

ex.en: The ambulance took the casualty to a nearby hospital.
Improved building standards can reduce the number of casualties when earthquakes strike densely populated urban areas.

en: a strong desire to learn or know about something

ex.en: Curiosity led me to open the dusty wooden box.
Schools should encourage children's curiosity by allowing them to investigate questions through practical experiments.

en: A strong metal made mainly from iron and some carbon

ex.en: The new bridge has a frame made of steel.
Recycling steel can reduce demand for raw materials and lower energy consumption in the construction industry.

en: To leave someone or something without intending to return.
vi: Từ bỏ, bỏ rơi; ngừng thực hiện giữa chừng

ex.en: We had to abandon our car in the snow.
ex.vi: Họ buộc phải từ bỏ kế hoạch leo núi vì bão tuyết ập đến.

ex.en: Cities should not abandon ambitious recycling programmes simply because initial participation rates are lower than expected.
ex.vi: Nhiều ngôi làng truyền thống đã bị bỏ hoang khi thanh niên di cư lên thành phố lớn.

col: abandon a plan — từ bỏ kế hoạch
abandoned building — tòa nhà bỏ hoang
tip: Trong IELTS Reading thường gặp "abandon a project/policy/traditional lifestyle".

en: A male ruler of an empire.

ex.en: The museum displays a robe once worn by an emperor.
The emperor expanded trade routes, allowing goods and cultural practices to spread across the empire.

en: a brother or sister

ex.en: My younger sibling always borrows my favourite blue jacket.
Children with siblings may develop negotiation skills early by sharing toys and resolving disagreements at home.

en: Unfamiliar or very different from what someone knows or accepts

ex.en: The city's constant noise felt alien after our quiet village.
Teaching methods that seem alien to international students may require careful explanation and additional support from university staff.

en: to mix substances or qualities together

ex.en: Blend the bananas and milk until the mixture is smooth.
Successful urban developments blend modern facilities with traditional architecture to preserve a city's distinctive character.

en: a situation in which there is not enough of something

ex.en: A water shortage forced us to take shorter showers.
A shortage of affordable housing can force essential workers to live far from their workplaces.

en: A narrow-waisted flying insect that can sting.

ex.en: A wasp landed on the edge of my glass.
Although wasps are often considered pests, many species help control insects that damage agricultural crops.

en: Sudden brain damage caused by interrupted blood flow or bleeding.

ex.en: The cat purred while I stroked its soft fur.
Recognising the early symptoms of a stroke can help patients receive treatment before serious brain damage occurs.

en: A curved weapon with a string used to shoot arrows.

ex.en: She tied a neat bow around the gift box.
In some cultures, people bow when greeting others, while elsewhere a handshake is more common.

en: not wanted or received with pleasure

ex.en: The loud music was an unwelcome interruption during dinner.
For many residents, rising rents are an unwelcome consequence of rapid development in urban areas.

en: A shellfish with a rough shell, sometimes producing pearls.

ex.en: The oyster shell felt rough against my fingers.
Restoring oyster populations can improve coastal water quality because these shellfish filter particles from the surrounding water.

en: A place or equipment provided for a particular purpose.

ex.en: The new sports facility has a bright indoor pool.
Investing in local healthcare facilities can improve access to essential services for people in rural communities.

en: a person walking rather than travelling in a vehicle

ex.en: The driver stopped to let a pedestrian cross.
Wider pavements and safer crossings can protect pedestrians and encourage residents to walk instead of driving.

en: An agreement in which each side accepts less than originally wanted.

ex.en: We reached a compromise and shared the last biscuit.
Governments must find a compromise between expanding housing supply and protecting green spaces in densely populated cities.

en: to increase something as much as possible or use it fully

ex.en: We added shelves to maximize space in our tiny kitchen.
Cities should improve public transport to maximize access to employment while reducing dependence on private cars.

en: money paid for teaching at a school or university

ex.en: She works at weekends to help pay her tuition.
Rising university tuition fees may discourage students from disadvantaged backgrounds from pursuing higher education.

en: A shaped piece used to cover floors, walls, or roofs.

ex.en: One blue tile has cracked beside the kitchen sink.
Using locally produced roof tiles can reduce transport emissions and support traditional industries in rural areas.

en: to squeeze something tightly, often between a finger and thumb

ex.en: Pinch the pastry edges together to seal the pie.
As food prices rise, families on low incomes increasingly feel the pinch and reduce nonessential spending.

en: in a way that meets expectations or requirements

ex.en: The washing machine worked satisfactorily after the repair.
Public transport cannot function satisfactorily unless local authorities invest in regular maintenance and staff training.

en: able to spread between people, like an illness or emotion

ex.en: Her laughter was catching, and soon everyone was smiling.
Although enthusiasm can be catching, public health campaigns also need clear evidence to encourage lasting behavioural change.

en: to experience a process, change, or treatment
vi: Trải qua (quá trình, phẫu thuật, thay đổi)

ex.en: My uncle will undergo knee surgery early next week.
Many coastal cities will undergo significant changes as rising sea levels force governments to reconsider urban planning.

en: A ship designed to carry large quantities of liquid

ex.en: We watched a huge tanker sail into the harbour.
An accident involving an oil tanker can cause lasting damage to coastal ecosystems.

en: Sudden pain caused by a muscle tightening involuntarily.

ex.en: A sudden cramp in my calf stopped me swimming.
Excessively strict classroom rules may cramp students' creativity and discourage them from exploring unfamiliar ideas.

en: a reason for doing something

ex.en: Her motive for joining was simply to make friends.
Financial security is a major motive for many graduates who choose careers in established companies.

en: to give someone what they want or need

ex.en: A bowl of soup was enough to satisfy my hunger.
New housing developments must satisfy strict environmental standards before local authorities allow construction to begin.

en: A change that fixes an error, or the act of fixing it.

ex.en: I made a correction before sending the email.
Timely correction of factual errors helps news organizations maintain public trust and prevent misinformation from spreading.

en: to find or direct the way to a destination

ex.en: We used a map to navigate the narrow streets.
Clear website design helps users navigate public services and access essential information without unnecessary delays.

en: Evaluated the quality, value, extent, or importance of something.

ex.en: The mechanic assessed the damage before repairing my bicycle.
Students should be assessed through varied tasks rather than judged solely on their performance in final examinations.

en: Relating to sight or things that can be seen.

ex.en: The exhibition combines music with some stunning visual effects.
Teachers can use visual aids to make complex scientific concepts easier for younger students to understand.

en: to catch someone or something and prevent escape

ex.en: Rescuers captured the injured bird and gently examined its wing.
Wildlife researchers use remote cameras to capture animal behaviour without disturbing natural habitats.

en: a separate unit within a larger course of study

ex.en: We finished the photography module with an outdoor project.
Universities increasingly offer a compulsory module on digital skills to prepare students for changing workplace demands.

en: A tendency to become angry, or an angry mood.

ex.en: He lost his temper when the drawer jammed again.
Governments should temper enthusiasm for new technologies with careful consideration of their potential social consequences.

en: Able to use two languages, or involving two languages.

ex.en: Our bilingual neighbour speaks both English and Chinese fluently.
Bilingual education can help children maintain their cultural identity while developing skills for an increasingly connected world.

en: unwanted involvement in someone else's affairs or decisions

ex.en: I wanted to choose my clothes without anyone's interference.
Universities need protection from political interference to ensure that research findings remain independent and credible.

en: to become less strong, or make something less strong

ex.en: Too little sleep can weaken your ability to concentrate.
Persistent unemployment can weaken local economies by reducing household spending and discouraging business investment.

en: a wide street, often lined with trees

ex.en: We walked along a quiet avenue shaded by tall trees.
Online learning offers an important avenue for adults seeking new skills while remaining in full-time employment.

en: In most cases or on most occasions.

ex.en: Our neighbours typically walk their dog before breakfast.
Cities with reliable public transport typically experience less traffic congestion than those dependent on private cars.

en: smooth, attractive movement or behaviour

ex.en: The dancer moved across the stage with effortless grace.
A short grace period can help households manage unexpected delays in receiving their income.

en: Likely to move, fall, or collapse.

ex.en: This unstable chair wobbles whenever I sit on it.
An unstable economy can discourage investment and make long-term planning difficult for small businesses.

en: Able to strongly affect people's opinions, decisions, or actions.

ex.en: Her grandfather was an influential teacher in their village.
Scientific advisers can be influential in shaping government policies on public health and environmental protection.

en: Willingness to give money, time, or help freely.

ex.en: Thanks to your generosity, everyone has a warm coat.
Community projects often depend on the generosity of residents who contribute both money and valuable practical skills.

en: A plant with large, often trumpet-shaped flowers.

ex.en: A white lily opened beside our kitchen window this morning.
Urban gardens planted with lilies and other flowering species can provide attractive spaces for local residents.

en: Having large, strong muscles.

ex.en: The muscular swimmer lifted the heavy box easily.
Regular resistance training can improve muscular strength and help older adults maintain their independence.

en: A child or young person.

ex.en: A cheerful youngster helped me pick up the apples.
Community sports programmes give youngsters opportunities to develop teamwork skills and build friendships outside school.

en: a very strong interest in someone or something

ex.en: She watched the tiny fish with fascination for hours.
Children's fascination with wildlife can provide a valuable starting point for environmental education in primary schools.

en: A school or class for children beginning their education

ex.en: My daughter painted a bright yellow bird at kindergarten.
High-quality kindergarten education can develop children's social skills and prepare them for more structured learning.

en: A distinct period in a process of change or development.

ex.en: The kitchen repairs have entered their final phase.
During the initial phase of urban development, planners should prioritise affordable housing and reliable public transport.

en: a person who controls a machine or piece of equipment

ex.en: The crane operator carefully lowered the beam into place.
Every public transport operator should ensure that its services remain accessible to passengers with limited mobility.

en: Someone or something that causes great admiration or surprise

ex.en: We marvelled at the tiny bird's beautifully woven nest.
The new bridge is an engineering marvel that connects isolated communities and improves access to essential services.

en: to use rude or offensive words

ex.en: Please don't swear when the game goes wrong.
Witnesses must swear to tell the truth before giving evidence in many legal systems.

en: A short account presenting the main features of a subject.

ex.en: Our guide gave us an overview of the tour.
The opening section provides an overview of the main challenges facing renewable energy development.

en: the process of finding people to join an organisation

ex.en: Our cafe handles recruitment before the busy summer season.
Fair recruitment practices help employers attract talented applicants from a wide range of social backgrounds.

en: Not very serious, important, or large.

ex.en: The bike only needs a few minor repairs.
Minor changes to daily travel habits can collectively reduce pollution in densely populated urban areas.

en: To examine facts carefully to discover what happened or why.

ex.en: A plumber came to investigate the strange noise upstairs.
Researchers are investigating how access to green spaces affects the mental health of urban residents.

en: To make something clear through examples or evidence.

ex.en: She used two jars to illustrate the difference.
These findings illustrate how access to public transport can improve employment opportunities in disadvantaged communities.

en: Deserving great admiration or bringing honour and pride.

ex.en: We spent a glorious afternoon swimming in the lake.
Museums should examine difficult historical events as carefully as they celebrate a nation's glorious achievements.

en: A list of things to check or do

ex.en: I use a checklist when packing for a trip.
A standard safety checklist can help hospital staff reduce avoidable errors during routine medical procedures.

en: easy to understand or do, without complications

ex.en: The recipe is straightforward, even for a beginner.
Governments should make recycling procedures straightforward so that more households can participate without unnecessary confusion.

en: To rub skin with fingernails, often to relieve itching.

ex.en: Please don't scratch that bite; it will get worse.
Even a small scratch on a reusable container can make it harder to clean effectively.

en: a glass or plastic building that keeps growing plants warm

ex.en: We grow tomatoes in the greenhouse throughout the winter.
Greenhouse cultivation can extend growing seasons, although heating these structures may require considerable amounts of energy.

en: The ability to achieve results without wasting time, energy, or resources

ex.en: Organising my tools improved the efficiency of my work.
Improving energy efficiency in public buildings can reduce government spending and lower greenhouse gas emissions.

en: united or closely connected as a whole

ex.en: Regular practice helped us become a more cohesive team.
Shared public spaces can help build cohesive communities by encouraging interaction among people from different backgrounds.

en: The main outer body of a ship or boat.

ex.en: We painted the boat's hull blue before launching it.
Improved hull designs can reduce fuel consumption by allowing ships to move through water with less resistance.

en: a document describing a school or university for potential students

ex.en: I checked the college prospectus for photography courses.
A university prospectus should provide accurate information about tuition fees, course content, and available student support.

en: A fourteen-line poem following a particular rhyme and rhythm pattern.

ex.en: She read a sonnet aloud beside the open window.
Studying a sonnet helps students understand how formal constraints can encourage creative expression in literature.

en: The education of boys and girls together in the same institution.

ex.en: My grandparents first experienced coeducation at their village school.
Supporters of coeducation argue that learning together helps boys and girls develop mutual respect.

en: An official abroad who assists citizens and represents national interests

ex.en: The consul helped us after we lost our passports.
A consul may support citizens facing difficulties overseas and help strengthen commercial links between countries.

en: Controlling people or situations unfairly for personal advantage.

ex.en: She recognised his emotional manipulation and refused to feel guilty.
The manipulation of survey results can mislead policymakers and reduce public trust in scientific research.

en: Happening or existing at the same time

ex.en: Two concurrent meetings meant I had to choose one.
Concurrent improvements in housing and public transport can make urban development more inclusive and sustainable.

en: Praise someone, often insincerely, to gain their favour.

ex.en: That blue jacket really flatters you in this light.
Advertisements often flatter consumers by suggesting that choosing a particular product demonstrates intelligence or good taste.

en: Interfere in other people's affairs without being invited.

ex.en: Please don't meddle in how I arrange my room.
Parents who constantly meddle in their children's decisions may prevent them from developing confidence and independence.

en: the act of thinking deeply and quietly about something

ex.en: He sat by the lake in quiet contemplation.
Public gardens offer urban residents valuable opportunities for quiet contemplation away from the pressures of daily life.

en: the level at which something starts happening or changes

ex.en: My brother has a much higher pain threshold than me.
Raising the income threshold for financial assistance would allow more low-paid workers to receive support.

en: To be the parts that form a whole

ex.en: Vegetables constitute most of the food in our fridge.
Rising housing costs constitute a major barrier to financial independence for young adults in large cities.

en: Happening or provided before a surgical operation.

ex.en: The nurse explained my preoperative checks before tomorrow's surgery.
Thorough preoperative assessment helps medical teams identify potential risks and plan appropriate care for each patient.

en: Existing as a natural or essential part of something.

ex.en: Even simple home repairs come with some inherent risks.
Policymakers must recognise the inherent limitations of economic growth as a measure of social progress and wellbeing.

en: based on observation or experiments rather than theory alone

ex.en: Our garden trial provided empirical evidence that compost helps plants.
Education policies should be supported by empirical research rather than assumptions about how children learn.

en: An area beside a sea, lake, or river, especially in towns.

ex.en: We walked along the waterfront after an early dinner.
Redeveloping the waterfront can create attractive public spaces, provided that existing residents are not forced to leave.

en: To share out or spread something again in a different way.

ex.en: We redistributed the blankets so everyone had one.
Progressive taxation can redistribute wealth and help governments fund essential services for disadvantaged communities.

en: the act of following a rule, law, or request

ex.en: The inspector checked our kitchen for compliance with hygiene rules.
Regular inspections can improve compliance with environmental regulations and reduce pollution from industrial facilities.

en: Not genuine, or intended to deceive people

ex.en: His phony smile disappeared as soon as we left.
Consumers should be cautious about phony online reviews that exaggerate the benefits of health products.

en: with great care and attention to every detail

ex.en: She meticulously cleaned each tiny part of the watch.
Researchers must meticulously record their procedures so that other teams can reproduce and verify the results.

en: shaped like a ball

ex.en: A spherical lamp hung above the dining table.
Researchers use spherical particles of different sizes to investigate how pollutants move through water filtration systems.

en: A detailed description of how something must be designed or made.

ex.en: Check the specifications before buying a new laptop.
Clear building specifications help ensure that new housing meets safety standards and uses energy efficiently.

en: Very serious or intense.

ex.en: The village faced an acute water shortage last summer.
An acute shortage of affordable housing forces many young workers to live far from their workplaces.

en: To allow fresh air to enter and circulate through somewhere.

ex.en: Open both windows to ventilate the kitchen after cooking.
Schools should ventilate classrooms regularly to improve indoor air quality and create healthier learning environments.

en: A small system showing the features of a larger one.

ex.en: Our busy kitchen is a microcosm of family life.
A diverse urban neighbourhood can serve as a microcosm of the wider society's opportunities and challenges.

en: Consideration of past events, often with a changed understanding.

ex.en: In retrospect, packing extra socks was a brilliant idea.
In retrospect, investing earlier in public transport could have prevented many of the city's current traffic problems.

en: make an action or process easier
vi: Tạo điều kiện thuận lợi, hỗ trợ

ex.en: These sliding doors facilitate access for people using wheelchairs.
Digital platforms can facilitate collaboration between students in different countries, allowing them to exchange ideas more easily.

en: to happen again, especially repeatedly or after an interval

ex.en: If these headaches recur, please speak to your doctor.
Traffic congestion will continue to recur unless cities address the underlying causes of excessive car use.

en: to remove a ruler or government from power

ex.en: The film follows citizens who overthrow an unfair ruler.
Economic hardship can weaken public support for a government and encourage attempts to overthrow it.

en: a substance burned to produce a pleasant smell

ex.en: A thin trail of smoke rose from the incense.
Burning incense indoors can affect air quality, particularly in small rooms with inadequate ventilation.

en: Very unusual and unexpected

ex.en: A freak hailstorm covered our garden in white ice.
A freak weather event can expose weaknesses in urban infrastructure and disrupt essential public services.

en: Making illegal copies of documents or artworks; such a copy.

ex.en: The painting in the shop was a forgery.
Museums employ specialists to detect forgery and protect the public from misleading claims about historical objects.

en: the upper edge of a cup, bowl, or other container

ex.en: She filled my cup to the brim with tea.
Community centres brimming with activity can strengthen social connections and reduce isolation among older residents.

en: Likely to experience something, especially something unpleasant.

ex.en: These old pipes are liable to burst in winter.
Employers may be held liable for injuries caused by unsafe conditions in the workplace.

en: To send someone or something to a particular destination.

ex.en: The shop dispatched my new shoes this morning.
Local authorities should dispatch emergency teams quickly when severe flooding threatens homes and essential infrastructure.

en: The arrangement of objects in a straight line or correct position.

ex.en: The mechanic checked the alignment of my front wheels.
Closer alignment between school curricula and workplace needs could improve employment prospects for young graduates.

en: Someone who supports government based on the people's choices

ex.en: As a democrat, she wants everyone to have a vote.
A committed democrat should defend fair elections even when the results favour a competing political party.

en: a desire to hurt someone or cause them trouble

ex.en: There was no malice in his teasing smile.
Schools should distinguish between careless remarks and comments made with malice when addressing conflicts among students.

en: Official confirmation that someone or something meets required standards.

ex.en: The swimming instructor proudly showed us her new certification.
Independent certification helps consumers identify products that meet recognised environmental standards throughout the production process.

en: needed for a particular purpose

ex.en: She has the requisite skills to repair this bicycle.
Applicants without the requisite qualifications may benefit from training programmes designed to improve access to skilled employment.

en: Dishonest behaviour intended to make someone believe something false.

ex.en: His deceit became clear when we opened the empty box.
Deceit in advertising can damage consumer trust and create unfair advantages for companies that misrepresent their products.

en: A temporary stop to an activity or someone's participation

ex.en: The storm caused the suspension of all ferry services.
The temporary suspension of construction work allowed researchers to assess the project's impact on local wildlife.

en: To spread through or occupy a place in unwanted numbers.

ex.en: Weeds have overrun the garden since our neighbours moved away.
Major infrastructure projects often overrun their budgets when planners underestimate material costs and construction delays.

en: playing an important part in making something happen

ex.en: Your advice was instrumental in helping me find work.
Investment in public transport has been instrumental in reducing traffic congestion in several major cities.

en: Unfair treatment of people to gain benefits from their work

ex.en: The workers demanded fair wages and protection from exploitation.
The uncontrolled exploitation of natural resources can damage ecosystems and undermine the livelihoods of communities that depend on them.

en: A drug used to calm people or animals and reduce anxiety.

ex.en: The vet gave the frightened horse a tranquilizer.
Doctors should carefully assess the risks before prescribing a tranquilizer to a patient with persistent anxiety.

en: Most common or influential at a particular time or place.

ex.en: The prevailing mood at dinner was one of relief.
The prevailing view among urban planners is that reliable public transport can reduce dependence on private cars.

en: A short period when activity or noise becomes less intense.

ex.en: We stepped outside during a lull in the rain.
A temporary lull in economic activity may give businesses time to review their long-term strategies.

col: lull someone into a false sense of security

en: extremely unpleasant or offensive

ex.en: An obnoxious passenger played loud music throughout the journey.
Obnoxious behaviour on public transport can discourage commuters from using otherwise convenient and affordable services.

en: Hang or bend down, often from weakness or tiredness.

ex.en: The flowers began to droop in the afternoon heat.
During prolonged droughts, leaves often droop as plants lose water and struggle to maintain their structure.

en: Speed in acting, often without enough care or thought.

ex.en: In my haste, I left my keys on the table.
Policies developed in haste may overlook the needs of vulnerable groups and create additional social problems.

en: to release sweat through your skin, especially when hot

ex.en: I began to perspire while carrying the heavy boxes.
People perspire more during intense exercise because the body needs to release excess heat.

en: The supply of water to land so crops can grow.

ex.en: The farm's irrigation system keeps these vegetables growing.
Efficient irrigation can increase crop yields while reducing water consumption in regions affected by drought.

en: To officially choose someone or something for a particular purpose.

ex.en: We designated one cupboard for all our cleaning supplies.
Local authorities should designate more urban land as protected green space to improve residents' quality of life.

en: to become smaller or weaker, or make something so

ex.en: The pain in my ankle gradually diminished overnight.
Investment in reliable public transport can diminish dependence on private cars and improve air quality in crowded cities.

en: The middle of a place, group, activity, or situation.

ex.en: We found a quiet garden in the midst of town.
In the midst of rapid urban growth, planners must preserve accessible green spaces for residents.

en: The universe considered as a complete, ordered system.

ex.en: Looking through the telescope made me curious about the cosmos.
Studying the cosmos helps scientists investigate how galaxies formed and how the universe has changed over time.

en: stay hidden, often waiting to do something

ex.en: A cat lurked behind the sofa, watching my shoelaces.
Security risks may lurk in outdated software, making regular system updates essential for protecting personal information.

en: Make sure that people obey a law or rule.

ex.en: The pool staff enforce strict rules about running indoors.
Governments must enforce environmental regulations consistently if they want industries to reduce pollution and protect public health.

en: Suggested or understood without being directly stated.

ex.en: Her welcoming smile was an implicit invitation to join.
Many workplaces have implicit expectations about overtime, which can make employees reluctant to leave on time.

en: Someone who helps opposing sides reach an agreement

ex.en: A mediator helped our neighbours settle their garden fence dispute.
An independent mediator can help employers and workers negotiate fair conditions without resorting to lengthy legal proceedings.

en: Someone arranging deals or buying goods to sell to others.

ex.en: We bought directly from the farmer, avoiding the middleman.
Online platforms allow small producers to reach consumers directly, reducing their dependence on a traditional middleman.

en: An official penalty intended to enforce rules or change behaviour.

ex.en: The club imposed a sanction for breaking its rules.
Economic sanctions may influence government policy, but they can also create hardship for ordinary citizens.

en: A short pointed knife, usually with two sharp edges.

ex.en: An ancient dagger lay inside the museum's glass case.
The discovery of a decorated dagger provides evidence of advanced metalworking skills in this ancient settlement.

en: Relating to electricity produced by the movement of water.

ex.en: We visited a hydroelectric dam during our mountain holiday.
Hydroelectric power can reduce dependence on fossil fuels, although large dams may disrupt river ecosystems.

en: continued effort despite difficulties or delays

ex.en: After weeks of practice, his persistence finally paid off.
The persistence of poverty suggests that economic growth alone cannot guarantee better living conditions for every household.

en: Usually, or when conditions are normal.

ex.en: We ordinarily eat outside, but today it is raining.
Public libraries ordinarily provide free internet access, helping residents who cannot afford a connection at home.

en: Happening immediately, with no noticeable delay.

ex.en: The relief was almost instantaneous when I removed my shoes.
Modern communication networks allow almost instantaneous exchanges of information between researchers working on different continents.

en: an event when one celestial body blocks another's light

ex.en: We watched the lunar eclipse from our garden last night.
Investment in digital services may eclipse spending on traditional infrastructure as economies become increasingly dependent on technology.

en: Get back something that belongs or previously belonged to you

ex.en: I returned to the station to reclaim my suitcase.
Coastal cities sometimes reclaim land from the sea to create space for housing and transport.

en: directly related to the matter being discussed

ex.en: Lena asked a pertinent question about the repair costs.
Evidence about local air quality is particularly pertinent to discussions of expanding public transport networks.

en: the projecting nose and mouth of an animal

ex.en: The pig pushed its snout through the wooden fence.
A pig's sensitive snout helps it locate food beneath the soil, supporting its natural foraging behaviour.

en: Too willing to believe what others say, even when untrue

ex.en: I was gullible enough to believe his ridiculous story.
Teaching media literacy can help gullible consumers recognise misleading advertisements and make better informed purchasing decisions.

en: A small, very sharp knife used in surgery or dissection.

ex.en: The surgeon placed the scalpel on a clean tray.
Medical students practise using a scalpel on artificial tissue before developing more advanced surgical skills.

A sermon can strengthen community ties by encouraging listeners to support vulnerable people and participate in local projects.

en: By which a particular result is achieved.

ex.en: We have an arrangement whereby we share the cooking.
Schools could introduce a system whereby older students provide academic support to younger pupils after lessons.

Cities can curb air pollution by improving public transport and encouraging residents to cycle.

en: The state of having no end or limit.

Stricter financial regulation can protect bank solvency and reduce the risk of a wider economic crisis.

Protecting tropical forests is essential for the survival of many primate species threatened by habitat loss.

The proposed station design is reminiscent of traditional architecture, helping the building blend into its historic surroundings.

Access to reliable internet has had a profound impact on educational opportunities in remote communities.

Early support for vulnerable families may reduce delinquent behaviour more effectively than harsher punishments alone.

Many countries have made significant strides in improving access to primary education over recent decades.

Although exclusivity agreements can encourage investment, they may also limit competition and raise prices for consumers.

Research in zoology helps scientists understand animal behaviour and design more effective strategies for protecting endangered species.

en: A form that differs slightly from other related forms.

A genetic variant may affect how individuals respond to certain medicines, making personalised treatment increasingly important.

en: a group living together and sharing possessions and responsibilities

ex.en: They live in a commune and grow vegetables together.
Living in a commune can reduce individual expenses, but shared decision-making requires patience and effective communication.

Exposure to exhaust fumes can worsen respiratory conditions, particularly among children living near busy roads.

ex.en: Henceforth, we will keep spare keys in this drawer.
The university announced that all new buildings would henceforth meet stricter environmental standards.

en: Carrying or holding a large amount of something.

ex.en: She arrived at the picnic laden with bags of food.
Trucks laden with construction materials contribute to congestion and increase road maintenance costs in rapidly expanding cities.

en: greatest in degree, amount, or intensity

Protecting patient privacy is of the utmost importance when hospitals introduce digital systems for storing medical records.

en: providing extra help or support when needed

Hospitals require auxiliary power systems to maintain essential medical services during unexpected electricity failures.

en: Find your position or become familiar with your surroundings.

Universities should orientate their support services towards the needs of students adjusting to life away from home.

en: Skill in making things, especially carefully by hand.

ex.en: The handmade chair shows beautiful craftsmanship in every joint.
Preserving traditional craftsmanship can support local economies while protecting cultural knowledge passed down through generations.

en: A tool with a sharp edge for cutting wood or stone.

ex.en: She used a chisel to shape the wooden bowl.
Traditional craftspeople use a chisel to create detailed patterns that preserve local artistic traditions.

en: loose rather than tightly stretched

ex.en: The tent rope was slack after the heavy rain.
When demand is slack, manufacturers may reduce working hours rather than dismiss experienced employees immediately.

en: Someone who lives in or uses a room, building, or vehicle.

Building regulations should ensure that every occupant can leave safely in the event of a fire.

en: Someone related to a person who lived in an earlier generation.

ex.en: Her descendants still live in the old family farmhouse.
Preserving traditional crafts allows descendants of local communities to maintain meaningful connections with their cultural heritage.

en: To argue that something is true.

ex.en: I contend that our kitchen needs a bigger table.
Some researchers contend that affordable public transport is more effective than road expansion in reducing urban congestion.

en: A person or organisation responsible for protecting or managing something.

ex.en: The custodian carefully locked the cabinet containing ancient coins.
Museums act as custodians of cultural heritage, preserving valuable objects for research and future generations.

en: Small or delicate enough to be difficult to notice

ex.en: The soup has a subtle hint of lemon.
Advertising can exert a subtle influence on consumers by associating products with desirable lifestyles.

en: To decrease very quickly and sharply.

Demand for private cars could plummet if cities offered reliable, affordable public transport throughout the day.

ex.en: My grandmother challenges the stereotype that older people dislike technology.
Schools should challenge gender stereotypes so that all students feel free to pursue their interests.

en: continuing for a long time or happening repeatedly

Persistent shortages of affordable housing can force young adults to delay leaving their family homes.

en: A long, narrow cut or hollow in a surface.

ex.en: Dust had collected in every groove of the wooden door.
The grooves in vehicle tyres channel water away, improving grip and reducing accident risks on wet roads.

en: A long, flat, thick piece of wood.

ex.en: We laid a plank across the muddy ditch.
Investment in affordable housing should be a central plank of any strategy to reduce urban inequality.

en: A politically organised community, especially one governed for public benefit.

ex.en: The islanders established a commonwealth with an elected council.
Members of the Commonwealth cooperate on education and development while maintaining their own independent governments.

en: to build something or put it in an upright position

ex.en: We erected our tent beside the lake before sunset.
Local authorities plan to erect temporary shelters for families whose homes were damaged by severe flooding.

en: To enjoy something greatly or eagerly anticipate doing it.

ex.en: I relish quiet mornings with tea and a book.
Many students relish the opportunity to study abroad because it exposes them to different cultures and perspectives.

en: To slow down or prevent a process or activity.

Fear of making mistakes can inhibit students from participating actively in classroom discussions and collaborative tasks.

Workers should not become pawns in disputes between powerful companies competing for control of essential services.

en: A policy of extending a country's power over other countries.

ex.en: We discussed imperialism after visiting the history museum yesterday.
The legacy of imperialism continues to influence economic relationships and debates about cultural identity in many societies.

en: a writer of short pieces exploring particular subjects

ex.en: The essayist described her childhood with warmth and humour.
An influential essayist can encourage readers to question social assumptions through personal reflection and careful argument.

en: To make something seem small by comparison.

The long-term costs of environmental damage may dwarf the immediate profits generated by industrial expansion.

en: an official responsible for a public service or commission

ex.en: The commissioner visited our neighbourhood to discuss road safety.
An independent commissioner should investigate public complaints and ensure that government agencies treat citizens fairly.

en: Destruction or killing on a very large scale.

Teaching students about the Holocaust can encourage critical reflection on prejudice, discrimination, and human rights.

en: A ceremony formally marking someone's start in an important public office.

ex.en: We gathered outside to watch the new president's inauguration.
The inauguration of the new railway marked a major step towards improving transport links between rural communities.

col: the inauguration of a new museum

en: Trees producing fruits such as oranges and lemons, or their fruits.

ex.en: We squeezed fresh citrus juice over the salad.
Rising temperatures may affect citrus production by increasing water demand and exposing orchards to new pests.

en: enthusiastic applause from an audience to show strong approval

ex.en: The young pianist received an ovation after her performance.
The orchestra received a standing ovation, demonstrating how live performances can create a powerful sense of community.

en: The state of being easily harmed, affected, or attacked.

ex.en: The storm exposed the vulnerability of our old roof.
Investing in flood defences can reduce the vulnerability of coastal communities to increasingly severe storms.

en: providing useful knowledge or helping someone understand something

Comparing different countries' recycling systems can be instructive for policymakers seeking to reduce household waste.

en: A house, flat, or other place where someone lives

ex.en: Their small dwelling overlooks a quiet stretch of river.
Every new dwelling should meet energy efficiency standards to reduce household costs and environmental damage.

en: A star-shaped symbol used to indicate a note or omission

ex.en: An asterisk beside the price points to extra delivery charges.
Researchers often use an asterisk in tables to indicate results that meet a particular statistical threshold.

en: Combine or join together to form a single whole.

ex.en: The two narrow paths merge just beyond the bridge.
Small businesses may merge to reduce operating costs and compete more effectively with larger companies.

en: the state of being widely known for something bad

ex.en: The restaurant gained notoriety for its dirty kitchen.
Some companies gain notoriety for environmental damage, making it harder for them to attract skilled workers.

en: A faint light, often shining unevenly

ex.en: A glimmer of candlelight escaped through the closed curtains.
Recent improvements in water quality offer a glimmer of hope for communities affected by industrial pollution.

en: an administrative system run by officials following established rules

ex.en: My aunt works within the city's large bureaucracy.
Reducing unnecessary bureaucracy could help small businesses obtain permits more quickly without weakening essential safety standards.

en: To make conflicting ideas, needs, or facts compatible

ex.en: We reconciled our different tastes by choosing a buffet.
Governments must reconcile the demand for affordable housing with the need to protect valuable green spaces.

en: The liquid part of blood in which blood cells float

ex.en: My cousin donates plasma at the local clinic.
Donated plasma contains proteins that can be used to produce treatments for certain immune system disorders.

en: not necessary and therefore best avoided

ex.en: Calling ahead saved us a needless trip across town.
Clear guidance on public services can prevent needless confusion and help residents access essential support.

en: To increase extremely quickly to a very high level.

ex.en: Our heating bills skyrocketed during the unusually cold winter.
Housing costs can skyrocket when population growth outpaces construction, making affordable accommodation increasingly difficult to find.

en: Relating to the gases surrounding Earth or another planet.

ex.en: We found an atmospheric café tucked behind the old theatre.
Changes in atmospheric conditions can affect agricultural production and increase the frequency of extreme weather events.

en: the process of starting an organisation or system

ex.en: The establishment of our local club brought neighbours together.
The establishment of protected marine areas can help restore fish populations and support coastal communities.

en: A written message sharing information within an organisation

ex.en: The manager sent a memorandum about our new working hours.
The two universities signed a memorandum of understanding to support joint research into renewable energy.

en: Relating to or required by a legal agreement.

ex.en: Fixing the heating is the landlord's contractual responsibility.
Employers should explain contractual obligations clearly so that workers understand their rights before accepting a position.

en: to praise someone or something, often publicly

ex.en: The coach commended Lina for helping her teammates.
Inspectors commended the school for providing additional support to students with different learning needs.

en: A lack of interest, concern, or emotional response.

ex.en: Her indifference surprised me when I shared my exciting news.
Public indifference to local elections can weaken accountability and reduce the quality of democratic representation.

en: To be inconsistent with another statement, fact, or piece of evidence.

ex.en: Your muddy shoes contradict your claim about staying indoors.
Recent findings contradict the assumption that longer working hours necessarily lead to higher levels of productivity.

en: To tell a story or describe a series of events.

ex.en: My grandfather loves to narrate stories from his childhood.
Local residents narrate their experiences in the documentary, offering valuable insights into urban change.

en: objects made of glass, especially drinking vessels or laboratory equipment

ex.en: Please wrap the glassware carefully before packing the box.
Reusable glassware can reduce waste in laboratories, provided that appropriate cleaning and safety procedures are followed.

en: relating to a province or its administration

ex.en: She works at the provincial hospital near our home.
Provincial governments can adapt national education policies to meet the specific needs of local communities.

en: To imagine a possible future situation or event.

Urban planners envisage a future in which most residents can reach essential services on foot.

en: Respect and admiration for someone.

ex.en: Her neighbours hold her in esteem for her kindness.
Teachers who treat students fairly often earn the lasting esteem of their local communities.

en: relating to courts, judges, or the administration of justice

ex.en: The lawyer explained the judicial process to our family.
An independent judicial system helps protect individual rights and ensures that governments remain accountable.

en: To keep something within particular limits

ex.en: Please confine your muddy boots to the porch.
Researchers should not confine their investigation to wealthy neighbourhoods when studying access to public transport.

en: A material that conducts electricity less easily than most metals.

ex.en: My sister works at a factory making semiconductor chips.
Investment in semiconductor manufacturing is essential for developing reliable supplies of components used in modern electronic devices.

en: A lack of enough of something necessary.

ex.en: A blood test revealed that I had an iron deficiency.
Nutritional deficiency among children can affect physical growth and reduce their ability to concentrate at school.

en: To burn a surface slightly or damage it with heat

ex.en: The hot iron scorched my favourite cotton shirt.
Prolonged heatwaves can scorch crops, reducing agricultural yields and threatening food supplies in vulnerable regions.

en: The matching arrangement of parts on opposite sides.

ex.en: The butterfly's open wings show beautiful symmetry in the sunlight.
Architects often use symmetry to create buildings that appear balanced and visually pleasing to visitors.

en: The inability to read and write.

ex.en: Evening classes helped my grandfather overcome illiteracy and read independently.
Reducing adult illiteracy can improve employment opportunities and enable more people to participate fully in society.

en: An event causing severe damage, suffering, or distress.

ex.en: The flood was a calamity for the whole village.
Effective emergency planning can reduce the human and economic costs of a natural calamity.

en: Managing relations between countries through discussion and negotiation.

ex.en: The two countries solved their disagreement through diplomacy.
Effective diplomacy can help neighbouring countries manage shared water resources without resorting to conflict.

en: the movement of people or goods between places

ex.en: The glasses broke while they were in transit.
Investment in public transit can reduce traffic congestion and improve access to employment in growing cities.

en: Not easily damaged or affected by something.

ex.en: These boots are resistant to water and easy to clean.
Some bacteria have become resistant to common antibiotics, making infections more difficult to treat.

en: payment given back for money someone has spent

ex.en: Keep your train ticket to claim reimbursement from work.
Providing reimbursement for travel expenses can make professional training more accessible to employees from low-income households.

en: the highest social class, traditionally holding inherited titles and privileges

ex.en: This grand house once belonged to the local aristocracy.

en: a large collection of different things

ex.en: The bakery displayed a colourful array of cakes.
Modern universities offer a wide array of courses to meet the demands of a changing labour market.

en: Something that happens before and introduces a more important event.

ex.en: Our short walk was a prelude to a lovely picnic.
Investment in reliable internet infrastructure is often a prelude to broader economic development in rural regions.

ex.en: The washing machine's strange noises continue to perplex me.
Conflicting dietary advice can perplex consumers who are trying to make healthier food choices.

en: The total weight of something expressed in tons.

ex.en: The driver checked the truck's tonnage before crossing.
The total tonnage of waste sent to landfill has declined since the city introduced recycling programmes.

Limited access to reliable internet can hinder educational progress among students living in remote rural communities.

ex.en: The dusty attic underwent a transformation into a cosy bedroom.
Investment in renewable energy could accelerate the transformation of industrial regions into centres of sustainable production.

ex.en: He gave a sheepish smile after spilling his juice.

The regularity of public transport services strongly influences whether commuters choose buses over private cars.

en: To move smoothly and easily, often without much noise.

ex.en: The swan glided across the pond towards the reeds.
Large birds conserve energy by gliding on rising air currents rather than continuously flapping their wings.

en: showing little interest or concern

en: the complete removal or destruction of something harmful

The eradication of infectious diseases requires sustained investment in vaccination programmes and public health infrastructure.

en: a person's usual emotional nature and way of reacting

Residents heard sirens wailing throughout the night as emergency teams responded to the severe flooding.

Understanding adverbial clauses helps language learners express relationships between events more precisely in academic writing.

en: a sculpture showing a person's head, shoulders, and upper chest

ex.en: A marble bust stood beside the museum entrance.
Displaying a bust of a local artist can help museums connect visitors with their community's cultural history.

en: a group of symptoms that occur together in a condition

ex.en: The doctor explained how the syndrome affects sleep.
Early recognition of a syndrome can help healthcare professionals provide appropriate support and manage symptoms more effectively.

en: An Australian egg-laying mammal with a flat bill and webbed feet.

ex.en: We watched a platypus swimming quietly near the riverbank.
Protecting rivers from pollution is essential for the survival of the platypus and other freshwater animals.

en: To talk with someone and exchange thoughts.

ex.en: We conversed quietly while waiting for the train.
Language exchange programmes allow students to converse with native speakers and develop confidence in unfamiliar social situations.

en: the act of carrying out a plan, order, or task

ex.en: The picnic plan was simple, but its execution proved tricky.
Successful execution of environmental policies requires adequate funding, clear responsibilities, and consistent monitoring by public authorities.

en: Almost certainly, or as one confidently expects.

en: A conclusion reached from evidence rather than direct statements.

ex.en: Her muddy boots supported my inference about her morning walk.
Researchers should avoid drawing a firm inference from a small sample without considering alternative explanations.

en: to make pain, suffering, or a problem less severe

ex.vi: Các chương trình giáo dục miễn phí đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc xóa đói giảm nghèo.

alleviate pressure — giảm bớt áp lực
tip: Phân biệt: "alleviate" dùng cho vấn đề/nỗi khổ (poverty, traffic congestion, pain).

en: relating to written words or the wording of a document

ex.en: The editor made several textual changes to my story.
Students should support their interpretations with textual evidence rather than rely solely on personal reactions to a novel.

en: An outward appearance or slight degree of a particular quality

ex.en: I tidied the cushions to restore some semblance of order.
After severe flooding, reopening schools can help communities regain a semblance of normality while essential infrastructure is repaired.

en: Showing that something exists or is likely to be true.

ex.en: These dark clouds are indicative of an approaching storm.
Rising demand for public transport may be indicative of changing attitudes towards car ownership in urban areas.

en: an instrument that measures air pressure

Consumer confidence is often regarded as a useful barometer of a country's overall economic health.

en: To give official permission for someone to do something.

ex.en: Only the manager can authorize a refund this large.
Local authorities may authorize new housing developments only after assessing their likely effects on traffic and public services.

en: Careful and sensible about risks and future consequences.

Prudent financial planning can help households cope with unexpected expenses during periods of economic uncertainty.

en: To become three times as much, or cause this increase.

ex.en: Our heating bills treble when the weather turns cold.
Investment in renewable energy could treble over the next decade if governments introduce stronger financial incentives.

en: Clever at getting what you want by deceiving others.

ex.en: The cunning fox waited until the dog fell asleep.
Cunning advertising tactics can persuade consumers to purchase products they neither need nor can afford.

en: A narrow stretch of water reaching into the land.

ex.en: We paddled into a quiet inlet sheltered by cliffs.
Coastal inlets provide sheltered habitats for marine species, but pollution can seriously damage these fragile ecosystems.

en: To grow strongly or develop successfully.

ex.en: These herbs flourish on our warm, sunny kitchen windowsill.
Small businesses are more likely to flourish when local governments provide affordable premises and reliable public transport.

ex.en: The coarse wool scratched my neck all afternoon.
Coarse particles in urban air can irritate the lungs and worsen existing respiratory conditions among vulnerable residents.

en: Opposite in direction, order, or effect

ex.en: Our free time and workload have an inverse relationship.
The study found an inverse relationship between regular physical activity and reported stress levels among office workers.

en: A point just before something happens, especially something bad.

ex.en: Their little shop was on the brink of closing.
Prolonged drought has pushed several rural communities to the brink of a severe food crisis.

en: Only, with nothing or nobody else involved.

Schools should not judge students solely on examination results, since practical skills also matter.

en: To deliberately avoid someone or something.

Some graduates shun corporate careers because they value personal independence more than a high salary.

en: The act of formally proposing someone for a position or award.

en: To the extent that something is true or possible.

ex.en: I'll help insofar as my busy schedule allows.
Online learning is effective insofar as students have reliable internet access and receive adequate support from teachers.

ex.en: The club bans anyone who tries to molest guests.
Public transport authorities should provide clear reporting procedures for passengers targeted by individuals who molest others.

en: to divide something into smaller parts or groups

ex.en: We subdivided the drawer with small wooden dividers.

en: To separate things that have become twisted or caught together.

en: Angry because something seems unfair or insulting.

ex.en: She was indignant when someone pushed ahead in the queue.

en: not having enough of something necessary

ex.en: The doctor said my diet was deficient in iron.
Communities with deficient healthcare services often face greater difficulties in preventing disease and supporting older residents.

en: very particular about small details and difficult to please

en: Move or remove something with a quick, light movement.

en: Able to read and write.

ex.en: She became literate after attending evening classes for adults.
Schools should ensure that students are digitally literate so they can evaluate online information critically.

en: Made so that water cannot enter or escape

Governments need watertight regulations to prevent companies from avoiding responsibility for environmental damage caused by their operations.

en: An animal or plant at a very early developmental stage

ex.en: We could see the chick embryo inside the egg.
Researchers study how environmental conditions affect embryo development to improve the breeding of endangered species.

en: Describe someone or something in a false or misleading way

ex.en: That photograph misrepresents the size of our tiny kitchen.
Advertisements can misrepresent the environmental benefits of products, making it harder for consumers to make informed decisions.

en: Someone who hoards money and strongly dislikes spending it.

ex.en: That miser refuses to replace his broken kitchen chair.

en: To react with oxygen, or lose electrons in a chemical reaction.

ex.en: The cut apple began to oxidize and turn brown.
